Who among these is an astronomer?
Annie Jump Cannon is an astronomer.
Which of these is a mathematician?
Michael Atiyah is a mathematician. Sir Michael Francis Atiyah (22 April 1929 – 11 January 2019) was a British-Lebanese mathematician specialising in geometry.
What is the atomic number of Tellurium?
Tellurium is a chemical element; it has the symbol Te and atomic number 52.
What is the atomic number of Manganese?
Manganese is a chemical element; it has the symbol Mn and atomic number 25.
In what year was Karl Marx born?
Karl Marx: Born in Trier in the Kingdom of Prussia, Marx earned a doctoral degree in philosophy from the University of Jena in 1841.
In what year was Benzene discovered?
Benzene is an organic chemical compound with the molecular formula C6H6.
Perl: Larry Wall. Perl is a high-level, general-purpose, interpreted, dynamic programming language.
IAI Kfir: Israel Aerospace Industries Ltd.
In which country is Thalidomide scandal?
Thalidomide scandal: Germany. It was introduced as a sedative and medication for morning sickness without having been tested on pregnant women.
Who is credited with discovering Flerovium?
Flerovium: Joint Institute for Nuclear Research. Flerovium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Fl and atomic number 114.
Who is credited with discovering Hypochlorous acid?
Hypochlorous acid: Antoine Jérôme Balard. Hypochlorous acid is an inorganic compound with the chemical formula ClOH, also written as HClO, HOCl, or ClHO.
Who is credited with discovering Gallium?
Gallium: Paul-Émile Lecoq de Boisbaudran. Gallium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ga and atomic number 31.
A King's College Cambridge graduate who earned a Princeton doctorate in 1938, he later joined Britain's wartime codebreaking effort and pioneered theoretical computing — who was he?
Alan Turing (23 June 1912 - 7 June 1954) was an English mathematician, computer scientist, logician, cryptanalyst, philosopher and theoretical biologist.
One of Ptolemy's original 48 and among the largest in the sky, this autumn constellation is named for a mythical princess chained to a rock for the sea monster Cetus — which one?
Andromeda (constellation) is one of the 48 constellations listed by the 2nd-century Greco-Roman astronomer Ptolemy, and one of the 88 modern constellations.

In 2003, this American mountaineer amputated his own trapped forearm with a dull pocket knife after five days pinned by a boulder in a Utah canyon, then rappelled and hiked miles to safety — who is he?

Aron Ralston (born October 27, 1975) is an American mountaineer, mechanical engineer, and motivational speaker, known for surviving a canyoneering accident in 2003 by cutting off part of his own right arm.
Which SI unit of radioactivity honors the scientist who co-discovered the phenomenon alongside the Curies?
Becquerel (symbol: Bq) is the unit of radioactivity in the International System of Units (SI).

Native to eastern North America with resident populations as far north as Newfoundland, this crested songbird in the crow family has a black, U-shaped collar around its neck and a mostly white chest — name it?
Blue jay (Cyanocitta cristata) is a passerine bird in the family Corvidae, native to eastern North America.
This flammable, colorless alkane gas with the formula C4H10 takes its name from a Greek word for butter, via butyric acid — what is it?
Butane is an alkane with the formula C4H10. Butane exists as two isomers, n-butane, CH3CH2CH2CH3 and iso-butane, (CH3)3CH.
This root vegetable owes its typical orange color to beta-carotene, though heirloom varieties can be white, purple, or even black — what vegetable is it?
Born in 1847, this American wore three hats at once — psychologist, logician, and mathematician. Who was she?
Christine Ladd-Franklin (December 1, 1847 - March 5, 1930) was an American psychologist, logician, and mathematician.
With algorithms and data structures at its core and the theory of computation among its branches, which field studies computation, information, and automation?

Computer science is the study of computation, information, and automation. The theory of computation concerns abstract models of computation and general classes of problems that can be solved using them.
A law professor known for scholarship on retribution and criminal sentencing, this Harvard-trained academic was killed in 2014 in a murder-for-hire scheme linked to a custody dispute — who is he?

Dan Markel (October 9, 1972 - July 19, 2014) was a Canadian-born attorney and law professor who wrote various works on retribution in criminal law and sentencing with a focus on the role of punishment in the criminal justice system.

England-born but raised in Australia, this geologist did much of his real rock-hunting in the Flinders Ranges — though he's better remembered for braving the ice alongside Shackleton on the Nimrod Expedition; who was he?
Douglas Mawson (5 May 1882 - 14 October 1958) was an Australian geologist, Antarctic explorer, and academic.
This branch of medicine studies the body's hormone-secreting glands and the chemical messengers, called hormones, that regulate growth, metabolism, mood, and more — name the field?
Endocrinology (from endocrine + -ology) is a branch of biology and medicine dealing with the endocrine system, its diseases, and its specific secretions known as hormones.
Every member of this mammal family is an obligate carnivore with retractile claws and a powerful bite, from forest dwellers to desert hunters — which family is it?
Felidae is the family of mammals in the order Carnivora colloquially referred to as cats.
Most common in the hands and feet, this cold-exposure injury can lead to complications like hypothermia or compartment syndrome — what is it called?
Frostbite is an injury to skin or other living tissue that is allowed to freeze, especially affecting the fingers, toes, nose, ears, cheeks and chin.

This small freshwater fish, native to China and one of the world's most popular aquarium pets, has become an invasive pest after being released into wild waterways in North America and Australia — what fish is it?
Goldfish (Carassius auratus) is a freshwater fish in the family Cyprinidae of the order Cypriniformes.
Tapeworms, flukes, and roundworms burrowing into the gut and beyond all fall under this macroparasitic disease — a neglected tropical illness better known as worm infection. What is it?
Helminthiasis is any macroparasitic disease of humans and other animals in which a part of the body is infected with parasitic worms, known as helminths.
Dissolved in water it yields a notoriously corrosive acid, yet it's also the main industrial route to fluorine and a feedstock for Teflon-style polymers like PTFE — which colorless compound is it?
Hydrogen fluoride is an inorganic compound with chemical formula HF.

Acting as the eye's diaphragm in optical terms, this thin ring-shaped structure controls how much light reaches the retina by adjusting the pupil's size, and also determines a person's eye color — name this structure?

Iris (anatomy) (pl.: irides or irises) is a thin, ring-shaped structure in the eye in most mammals and birds that is responsible for controlling the diameter and size of the pupil, and thus the amount of light reaching the retina.

He wrote the first commercial anti-virus software in 1987 and ran twice for the Libertarian presidential nomination — yet later urged people to uninstall the very product that still bears his name. Who is he?
John McAfee (18 September 1945 - 23 June 2021) was a British and American computer programmer, businessman, and two-time U.S.
Endemic to New Zealand, this large, nocturnal, ground-dwelling parrot has owl-like forward-facing eyes and holds the title of the world's only flightless parrot — what bird is it?
Kākāpō (Mori:; pl.: kkp; Strigops habroptilus), sometimes known as the owl-parrot, is a species of large, nocturnal, ground-dwelling parrot of the superfamily Strigopoidea.
Believed to stem from genetic and hormonal disruption of the lymphatic system, this condition traps fat in the legs regardless of a woman's overall weight — what's the diagnosis?
Lipedema is a condition that is almost exclusively found in women and results in enlargement of both legs due to deposits of fat under the skin.
Transmitted by the bite of Anopheles mosquitoes, this infectious disease causes fever, fatigue, and headaches, and in severe cases can lead to seizures, coma, or death — name the disease?
Malaria is a mosquito-borne infectious disease that is transmitted by the bite of Anopheles mosquitoes.
Crushed leaves of this mint-family herb smell like spearmint, yet it has caused deaths when used as a traditional abortifacient — which species, also known as pennyroyal?

Mentha pulegium (European) pennyroyal, or pennyrile, also called mosquito plant and pudding grass, is a species of flowering plant in the mint family, Lamiaceae, native to Europe, North Africa, and the Middle East.
In 1812 Étienne Geoffroy grouped the apes with the Cercopithecidae under the name Catarrhini, or "Old World" members of this familiar simian group — what common name is it?
Monkey is a common name that may refer to most mammals of the infraorder Simiiformes, also known as simians.

Encompassing several types of kidney inflammation affecting the glomeruli, tubules, or nearby interstitial tissue, this general medical term falls under the broader category of nephropathy — what's the condition?
Nephritis is inflammation of the kidneys and may involve the glomeruli, tubules, or interstitial tissue surrounding the glomeruli and tubules.
Concerned with the most fundamental concept of all — being — this branch of metaphysics distinguishes non-repeatable particulars from repeatable universals like 'green' — what is the field?
Ontology is the philosophical study of being.
Named for the extra copy of chromosome 13 found in affected cells, this condition — related to Down and Edwards syndromes — disrupts normal organ development — which syndrome?
Patau syndrome is a syndrome caused by a chromosomal abnormality, in which some or all of the cells of the body contain extra genetic material from chromosome 13.
This anxiety disorder involves an irrational, excessive, and persistent fear of a specific object or situation, often leading sufferers to go to great lengths to avoid it — what is it called?
Phobia is an anxiety disorder, defined by an irrational, unrealistic, persistent and excessive fear of an object or situation.
Named from the Greek for an infinite carbon chain it would ultimately become, this class of organic compounds strings together alternating single and triple bonds. What is it called?
Polyyne is any organic compound with alternating single and triple bonds; that is, a series of consecutive alkynes, (CC)n with n greater than 1.

Brought from China to Europe in the sixteenth century and popularized by the House of Orange in the Netherlands, this dog breed is known for its wrinkly, short-muzzled face and curled tail — name the breed?
Pug is a breed of dog with the physically distinctive features of a wrinkly, short-muzzled face, and curled tail.
Also called king's crown or Arctic root, this Arctic-growing perennial is widely sold as a supplement even though regulators say its health claims lack solid evidence — which plant?
Rhodiola rosea (commonly golden root, rose root, roseroot, Aaron's rod, Arctic root, king's crown, lignum rhodium, orpin rose) is a perennial flowering plant in the family Crassulaceae.
Having taught economics at the Catholic University of Asunción and once served as Paraguay's finance minister, this politician assumed his country's presidency in 2023 — who is he?
Santiago Peña (Spanish; born 16 November 1978) is a Paraguayan politician and economist who has served as the 52nd president of Paraguay since 2023.

Defined by the American Thoracic Society as a subjective, uncomfortable experience of breathing discomfort that can include chest tightness or a sense of effort to breathe — what is this sensation called?
Shortness of breath (SOB), known as dyspnea (in AmE) or dyspnoea (in BrE), is an uncomfortable feeling of not being able to breathe well enough.

Distinguished from relatives in its conifer family by four-sided needles attached singly to small peg-like structures on the twigs, this genus of about 37 evergreen tree species thrives across the Northern Hemisphere's boreal forests — what's the tree?

Spruce is a tree of the genus Picea, a genus of some 37 species of coniferous evergreen trees in the family Pinaceae, found in the northern temperate and boreal (taiga) regions of the Northern Hemisphere.
This Turkish businesswoman served as one of her father's chief advisers back in 2013, when he held the office of prime minister and later became Turkey's president — who is she?
Sümeyye Erdoğan (ne Erdoan; born 22 August 1985) is a Turkish businesswoman and the daughter of President Recep Tayyip Erdoan.
Shaped like a butterfly and located in the neck just below the Adam's apple, this endocrine gland's two lobes are joined by a thin band of tissue called the isthmus — name the gland?

Thyroid is an endocrine gland in vertebrates. The lower two thirds of the lobes are connected by a thin band of tissue called the isthmus (pl.: isthmi). The thyroid gland secretes three hormones: the two thyroid hormones – triiodothyronine (T3) and thyroxine (T4) – and a peptide hormone, calcitonin.

One of the two main forms of inflammatory bowel disease, this long-term condition inflames and ulcerates the colon and rectum, flaring up with abdominal pain and bloody diarrhea before quieting down again — what is it?
Ulcerative colitis (UC) is one of the two types of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), with the other type being Crohn's disease.
Belonging mostly to one family of long-snouted beetles, this group includes bark beetles and grain-damaging pests despite some members lacking the trademark snout — what are they?
Weevil are beetles belonging to the superfamily Curculionoidea, known for their very long snouts.

Unlike a user interface, which links a computer to a person, this software connection lets programs talk directly to each other — and the standard describing it is called its specification. What's the three-letter term?
API: Connection between computers or programs.
Nicknamed the 'killer' variety for its aggressive defense of the hive, this hybrid pollinating insect escaped Brazilian quarantine in 1957 and reached Texas by 1990 — which insect is it?
Africanized bee: Hybrid species of bee. The African honey bee was first introduced to Brazil in 1956 to increase honey production, but 26 swarms escaped quarantine in 1957.
Also called ramsons or bear leek, this bulbous woodland plant native to Eurasia is a wild cousin of onion and garlic — what is it?
Allium ursinum: Species of flowering plant in the family Amaryllidaceae.
Comprising more than 140 species across 16 genera, this small, oily forage fish is found everywhere from the Atlantic to the Black Sea — what is it?
First described by Linnaeus in 1753, this Old World vegetable — better known on dinner plates as celery — is also cultivated for a bulbous root form called celeriac. What is its scientific name?
From the Greek for 'lack of order,' this neurological sign involves loss of voluntary muscle coordination, often linked to cerebellum dysfunction — what is it called?
Ataxia: Neurological impairment of voluntary muscle movement.
The only mammals capable of true sustained flight, this group flies on long digits webbed with a thin membrane and makes up about 20% of all classified mammals — what are they?
Members of this warm-blooded class range from the 5.5 cm bee hummingbird to the 2.8 m ostrich, share toothless beaked jaws, and lay hard-shelled eggs — what are they?
Bird: Warm-blooded animals with wings and feathers.
Also nicknamed 'starflower,' this Mediterranean annual herb yields seed oil despite containing small amounts of toxic alkaloids — which plant?
Borage: Species of flowering plant in the family Boraginaceae.
Caused by heat, electricity, chemicals, friction, or radiation — and most often the result of scalding at home — what type of skin injury is classified from first- to higher-degree severity?
Burn: Injury to flesh or skin, often caused by excessive heat.
Nicknamed for its heart-shaped seed pods, this mustard-family weed is considered protocarnivorous because its seeds ooze a mucilage that traps nematodes — which species?
Capsella bursa-pastoris: Species of flowering plant in the mustard family.
Which biological process oxidizes nutrients using an electron acceptor such as oxygen to generate ATP, the universal energy currency of life?
Cellular respiration: Process of releasing energy from nutrients using inorganic electron acceptors.

The second-lightest halogen, this yellow-green gas is so reactive it has the highest electron affinity of any element and once fascinated medieval alchemists heating chloride salts — which element is it?
Chlorine: Chemical element with atomic number 17 (Cl)
Native to the Americas from Mexico to South America, this diurnal member of the Procyonidae family goes by the name 'quash' in Belize — what is it?

Known to NATO by the reporting name 'Mop' and to Canadian forces as the Canso, this WWII flying boat served every branch of the U.S. military and remained in some air forces into the 1980s — which aircraft?
Consolidated PBY Catalina: American 1930s flying boat.
Native to the Irano-Turanian region, this flowering plant's dried seeds season cuisines worldwide, despite no strong evidence backing its use in traditional medicine — which spice?
Cumin: Species of plant with seeds used as a spice.
This field statistically studies human populations — their size and makeup — through the interplay of births, deaths, and migration — what is it?
Demography: Study of human populations and their structures.
Descended from the African wild ass and domesticated some 5,000 to 7,000 years ago, which working equine still numbers over 40 million worldwide?
Donkey: Domesticated animal primarily used for transportation.
Known as aubergine or brinjal elsewhere, this purple, spongy fruit in the nightshade family is technically a berry despite usually being cooked as a vegetable — what is it?
A German Jew who fled the Nazi regime, this social psychologist and democratic socialist helped found a psychoanalytic institute in New York and was linked to the Frankfurt School — who is he?
Once widespread during the Pleistocene and later reintroduced by humans to its ancient range, which hoofed mammal species is native to Turkey and possibly Italy, the Balkans, and Rhodes?
European fallow deer: Species of hooved mammal. The European fallow deer (Dama dama), also known as the common fallow deer or simply fallow deer, is a species of deer native to Eurasia.
Also known as the bodhi tree, this species is revered in four South Asian religions as the tree beneath which Buddha is said to have reached enlightenment — which species?
Ficus religiosa: Species of fig. Ficus religiosa or sacred fig is a species of fig native to the Indian subcontinent and Indochina that belongs to Moraceae, the fig or mulberry family.
Known online by the alias TiAMO, this Swede co-founded a notorious file-sharing site and stood trial for it in 2009, a saga captured in the documentary TPB AFK — who is he?

Germany's first professor of experimental physics is remembered both for the tree-like electrical discharge patterns named after him and for the witty posthumous notebooks he called "waste books" — who was he?
Georg Christoph Lichtenberg: German scientist and satirist (1742–1799)

This German engineer invented the high-speed petroleum engine, working alongside his lifelong partner Wilhelm Maybach to build small, fast motors they hoped to mount on any kind of vehicle. Who was he?
Gottlieb Daimler: German engineer, industrialist and automotive pioneer (1834–1900)
Its name literally combines words for 'holy' and 'flatfish,' reflecting its popularity on Catholic holy days — this demersal fish is prized both as food and as a sport catch. Which fish?

Synthesized from the dried latex of the opium poppy, this opioid is used medically in some countries to relieve pain during childbirth or a heart attack — and its 'black tar' form is a crude, variable mix of morphine derivatives — what is it?
Heroin: Opioid analgesic and recreational drug.
The flowers of this shrub genus act as natural pH indicators, turning blue in acidic soil and pink in alkaline soil?
Designed in 1967 to replace the An-12 and haul heavy machinery into remote, poorly served regions, this four-engine Soviet airlifter earned the NATO name 'Candid' — what is it?
Ilyushin Il-76: Russian heavy four-engined military transport jet aircraft.
A Harvard chemistry professor who studied chlorophyll and helped develop poison gas in WWI, he later became Harvard's president and the first U.S. ambassador to West Germany — who is he?
Nicknamed "Marvellous Merchiston," this 16th-century Scottish laird discovered logarithms and popularized the decimal point — who was this mathematical wizard?
A biologist and botanist married four times — her last husband directed the Manhattan Project's Los Alamos lab — she was played by Emily Blunt in a 2023 film. Who was she?
Its lens-shaped seeds, usually two to a pod, are split and simmered into the dal that's a staple across the Indian subcontinent — which legume?
Lentil: Species of plant with edible seeds.
Nicknamed "Connie" and instantly recognizable by its triple tail and dolphin-shaped fuselage, which four-engined airliner was the first civil aircraft family to widely use a pressurized cabin?
Lockheed Constellation: Family of US airliners with 4 piston engines, 1943.
This age-related eye disease gradually damages the retina's central region, with a 'wet' form involving leaking blood vessels and a 'dry' form marked by deposits called drusen — what is it?
Macular degeneration: Vision loss due to damage to the macula of the eye.

Endemic to North America and known for long, upward-curving upper tusks with little to no lower tusks, this proboscidean's genus split from other elephant relatives at least 28 million years ago — which ancient beast?
Sold under the brand Glucophage, this first-line oral medication for type 2 diabetes is favored partly because it isn't associated with weight gain. What drug is it?
Metformin: Medication used to treat diabetes.
This synthetic prostaglandin medication treats stomach ulcers, induces labor, and — often paired with mifepristone — is used to end a pregnancy. What drug is it?
Misoprostol: Medication to induce abortion and treat ulcers.
Considered a cultural universal present in every human society, this medium arranges sound into harmony, melody, and rhythm through composition, improvisation, and performance — what is it?
Music: Form of art using sound.
Erected by entomologist Francis Walker back in 1855, this genus of moths belongs to the family Lasiocampidae — which genus?
Grown worldwide as ornamentals in ponds and known to gardeners simply as water lilies, this widespread genus of aquatic plants also includes species considered weeds — which genus?
Nymphaea: Genus of aquatic plants. Nymphaea is a genus of hardy and tender aquatic plants in the family Nymphaeaceae.
This surgical medical subspecialty treats the ear, nose, and throat — organs connected via the Eustachian tube — earning its specialists the nickname 'ENT surgeons.' What field is it?
Otorhinolaryngology: Medical specialty of the head and neck.

He joined the British Astronomical Association at age 11, compiled the Caldwell catalogue, and hosted the BBC's "The Sky at Night" — the longest-running TV series with its original presenter. Who was this English amateur astronomer?
Patrick Moore: English astronomer, broadcaster and writer (1923–2012)
Sold under the brand name Luminal, this WHO-recommended barbiturate treats epilepsy in children and can be given intravenously for status epilepticus — which drug?
Phenobarbital: Medication of the barbiturate type.
Injected by a mosquito's bite and multiplying first in the liver before invading red blood cells, this parasite genus is the cause of malaria — what is it?
Plasmodium: Genus of parasitic protists that can cause malaria.
Originating in Spain's Canary Islands, this large mastiff-type breed was historically used for guarding, herding sheep and cattle, and — legally until 1936 — dog fighting. Which breed?
Presa Canario: Spanish breed of dog. It originates in the Spanish autonomous community of the Canary Islands, and is found mostly in the islands of Gran Canaria and Tenerife.
Usually caused by E. coli spreading up the urinary tract, this kidney infection typically brings fever and flank tenderness, and can be prevented by urinating after sex — what condition is it?
Pyelonephritis: Inflammation of the kidney. It is typically due to a bacterial infection, most commonly Escherichia coli.
From a startled jump to a cat automatically reorienting itself mid-fall, this involuntary, split-second reaction runs through the nervous system without needing conscious thought — what's it called?
Reflex: Automatic, involuntary response to a stimulus.
Commonly called the dog rose, this variable climbing wild plant is native to Europe, northwest Africa, and western Asia — which species?
Also known as mucopolysaccharidosis type III, this rare genetic disorder is caused by the body's inability to break down certain sugar molecules called glycosaminoglycans — what is it called?

Sanfilippo syndrome: Rare metabolism disorder. Sanfilippo syndrome, also known as mucopolysaccharidosis type III (MPS III), is a rare lifelong genetic disease that mainly affects the brain and spinal cord.
Considered paradoxical by the ancient Greeks in Zeno's puzzle about motion, what term describes an infinite sum of terms added one after another, later made rigorous through the concept of a limit?
Series (mathematics): Infinite sum. In mathematics, a series is, roughly speaking, an addition of infinitely many terms, one after the other.
The sixth most abundant element in Earth's crust, this soft alkali metal carries symbol Na and pairs with chlorine as the ocean's most common dissolved element — what is it?
Sodium: Chemical element with atomic number 11 (Na)
Named in 1880 from Greek words meaning 'bunch of grapes,' this genus of spherical, grape-clustered bacteria can grow with or without oxygen — which genus?
Striking suddenly and resolving — one way or another — within 8 to 10 hours, this mysterious epidemic first hit England in 1485 and vanished after a final outbreak in 1551 — what was it called?
Sweating sickness: Contagious disease in Europe, 1485–1551.
An Australian-American math prodigy who won the Fields Medal in 2006, he proved a famous theorem on prime numbers with Ben Green in 2004. Who is he?
Terence Tao: Australian and American mathematician (born 1975)

Proposing an information-management system in March 1989, this English computer scientist implemented the first web browser and web server and founded the organization that still oversees the web's standards — who is he?

Endemic to New Zealand and often mistaken for a lizard, this reptile is the sole surviving member of an order that thrived back in the Mesozoic era — its Māori name means 'peaks on the back.' What is it?
Tuatara: Species of reptile. The tuatara (Māori: [ˈtʉ.a.ta.ɾa]; Sphenodon punctatus) is a species of reptile endemic to New Zealand.

Nicknamed the 'vampire fish' for feeding on the blood of larger fish through their gills, this tiny Amazonian catfish is infamous for an alleged, rare habit of entering human body openings — what is it?
Vandellia cirrhosa: Species of ray-finned fish.
Native to the Baltic, Black, and Caspian Sea basins, this large freshwater fish's range now stretches from the UK to western China — which species?
Wels catfish: Species of fish. It has been introduced to several countries in Western Europe, Mediterranean and Asia as a prized sport fish.
Ukraine's first female prime minister, she co-led the Orange Revolution and later led the Batkivshchyna party while championing EU integration — who is she?
Yulia Tymoshenko: Prime Minister of Ukraine (2005, 2007–2010)

The symbol for lead is Pb. Lead is a chemical element with the symbol Pb and atomic number 82.
